newsitem.title: ANGOLA: Angola to deport 18 S.Africans on Monday -embassy.
newsitem.headline: Angola to deport 18 S.Africans on Monday -embassy.

text.p: Eighteen South Africans, accused by police of working in the diamond areas without official work permits, are to be deported from Angola on Monday, a South African embassy official said on Sunday.

"I have spoken to the authorities who have agreed that they will be deported on Monday," Glen Fourie, the head of the South African embassy's consular section, told Reuters. The men were held at a Luanda prison over the weekend, pending deportation.

Fourie said some of the men were arrested at Saurimo in Lunda Sul province and the rest at N'Giva in Cunene province, where they were also accused of operating an illegal flight from Cape Town to Saurimo.
"They are also charged with not paying customs duties and taxes for equipment worth $2 million and for working in Angola on a visitor's visa," Fourie said.

Representatives of several South African mining companies who were meeting in Luanda at the weekend told Reuters they were in Angola seeking help from South African and Angolan authorities to get back equipment worth millions of dollars.

They accused generals and businessmen who own concessions in diamond-rich Lunda Norte of cheating their South African partners by having them pay for equipment which was "hijacked" once it arrived at the site.
One South African-based diamond company said that 10 of its workers were being held hostage in Lunda Norte by Angolan soldiers protecting a concession owned in part by generals.
An official from the Eurotech mining company in Luanda told Reuters its workers had been captured west of Camissombo where they had been mining on the Chicapa River.

"They are being held hostage in harsh conditions and food is running out. We can't get to them or to the equipment because the area is being guarded by troops," said the official, who asked not to be named.

"Their passports were taken and not returned by the Angolan partners (in the concession) for months. Now that we have the passports back, the visas are invalid and it will cost us $4,500 in fines," the official said.

One mining consultant said Pretoria should warn its citizens about the scam: "We cannot understand why the South African government has not warned business people in South Africa about what is going on in Angola."
